title: session-greedy-vs-frugal-bench-notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a working draft comparing two session allocation policies for our inference runtime: GREEDY (fill slots with long-lived sessions aggressively) vs FRUGAL (prefer compact packing, favor short-lived sessions to reduce idle KV cache pressure). Goal is to capture tradeoffs in tail latency, amortized cost per session, and cache hit behavior for conversational workloads.

Test harness and environment:
- Cluster: dedicated q8 pools (8xA100 equiv) in us-west1 staging.
- Model: open-llm-13b-fp16 (representative decoder-only workload).
- Traffic traces: three anonymized session traces derived from production: microchat (median 8 tokens/user turn), agent (median 40 tokens/turn, longer history), microburst (many short sessions with sudden spikes).
- Time window: 30 minute steady-state after warmup.
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p99 decode latency (ms), throughput (req/s), slot utilization (%), KV cache hit-rate (%), cost estimate (dollars per 100k requests using internal cost model).

High-level summary (draft):
- GREEDY reduces cold-starts for long conversations leading to ~12% lower p50 for agent traces, but increases p99 under microburst by ~18% because long-lived sessions hold slots and cause queuing amplification.
- FRUGAL yields better slot utilization across mixed traffic (up to +9% utilization), lower amortized cost per session for microchat style workload (~7% savings), and maintains tighter p99 in bursty scenarios.
- KV cache hit-rate: GREEDY benefits long-running agent flows (hit-rate +24% for agent), FRUGAL reduces global cache pressure improving hit-rate for short sessions (+6% for microchat).

Representative numbers (table):

Scenario | Policy | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | slot_util(%) | kv_hit(%) | cost_per_100k($)
--------|--------|---------|---------|---------|-------------|----------|-------------------
agent   | GREEDY | 120     | 210     | 420     | 62          | 78       | 1,320             
agent   | FRUGAL| 138     | 230     | 360     | 57          | 64       | 1,410             
microchat| GREEDY| 40      | 78      | 180     | 46          | 34       | 420               
microchat| FRUGAL| 44     | 82      | 150     | 55          | 40       | 390               
microburst| GREEDY| 95    | 260     | 580     | 38          | 28       | 920               
microburst| FRUGAL| 110   | 210     | 490     | 47          | 34       | 880               

Interpretation notes (working):
- Agent trace: GREEDY gives lower median latency because hot sessions keep KV cached and avoid prefix re-computation. The p99 is worse on GREEDY for mixed traffic where queuing builds behind long sessions.
- Microchat: FRUGAL reduces cost and p99 by freeing slots and enabling better packing; the increased p50 is small and acceptable for UX targets.
- Microburst: FRUGAL reduces queuing amplification by evicting idle long sessions earlier and admitting short spike handlers faster.

Ascii visualization (latency distribution sketch, relative):
- agent (GREEDY): p50=|####| p90=|#########| p99=|###################|
- agent (FRUGAL): p50=|#####| p90=|##########| p99=|#############|
- microchat (GREEDY): p50=|##| p90=|#####| p99=|##########|
- microchat (FRUGAL): p50=|###| p90=|######| p99=|########|

Key micro-observations (bullet list):
- Slot churn: FRUGAL triggers more slot churn (start/stop) but reduces average idle slot time by ~37% which correlates with cost savings on microchat.
- Warmup penalty: GREEDY requires fewer warmups for agent sessions but at the expense of headroom for sudden spikes.
- Admission latency: under FRUGAL admission for a short session during high load is ~12ms slower on average due to packing logic, but overall system p99 stays lower.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate with larger model variants (33B) — is the FRUGAL packing advantage preserved when KV sizes grow?
- Sensitivity to slot granularity: current experiments use 1-slot-per-session; need sweep for half-slot and multi-session-per-slot strategies.
- Client experience: run small A/B with conversation continuation to see if increased p50 in FRUGAL microchat impacts user satisfaction.
- Cost model tuning: current cost_per_100k uses internal amortization — link to cost model: CONFLUENCE-ENG-costing-v4 (TODO verify weights).

Operational suggestions (draft):
- For Dedicated tiers serving enterprise agent workloads, default to GREEDY with configurable eviction horizon to avoid p99 explosions during spike events.
- Offer FRUGAL as recommended default for public hosted Chat endpoints optimized for throughput/cost (PLG instantiation).
- Add an adaptive hybrid policy: start GREEDY for sessions that cross a token threshold (e.g., >256 tokens) then switch to FRUGAL heuristics when cluster contention > 70%.

Experiment artifacts and quick links:
- Raw traces: gs://redwood-inference-staging/bench/session-greedy-frugal/
- Jupyter: github.com/redwood/bench-notebooks/session-packing-sweep.ipynb
- Dashboards: /console/bench/session-packing/summary (requires prod-infra access)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working note, numbers are noisy across runs (stddev p99 can be 8–12%). Please do not ship these numbers outside eng without tagging as draft.
- If you want to reproduce: run harness v2.1 with env var PACK_POLICY = {greedy,frugal} and seed trace-ids from the traces folder.
